| CS-26H2-03 | **Agent-portal for top CSC flows**  (Backend + frontend) | Lighthouse Phase 2 HRN Strategy - reduce and simplify UX  Operational excellence | B2X and Salesforce |  | **Description:** Deliver the most used PG Client CSC agent use cases in a new web frontend. Replace the legacy PG SOAP API. No BDA usage. Use the project to further the goal of removing BDA. Simplify the architecture, replace or remove expensive integrations with third-party services, and move towards removing dependencies on Citrix and locally installed clients. **Deliveries:** New web frontend for top PG Client CSC agent use cases; new PG APIs ;  **Teams:** B2X (frontend), Backend (PG Api). **Goal:** By the end of Q3 2026, the new web Agent-portal serves the top-N most-used PG Client CSC flows as the default tool, replacing PG-backed paths. **Success:** >=80% of agent task starts in those flows happen in the portal;  BDA call volume for in-scope flows = 0; in-scope PG SOAP calls removed.   
 | Backend: 1 Frontend: 1 | Q3 2026 | **Post:** opens shared REST API surface to B2X and SF  | Use-case scope is the most-used CSC flows only; non-essential use cases stay in legacy PG Client until later. |
| CS-26H2-04 | Automate loading and IROPS tasks | Operational excellence | IROP and Loading |  | **Description:** Automate manual loading and IROPS tasks, as well as reducing the number of manual touchpoints in the booking flow. **Deliveries:** Tool for automation of selected loading and IROPS steps; reduced manual touchpoints in the booking flow. **Process owner:** IROP & Emergency Preparedness team. **Goal:** By the end of Q3 2026, the agreed subset of loading and IROPS steps runs as automation in the booking flow, eliminating manual touchpoints on those steps. **Success:** zero manual interventions on in-scope steps over a 4-week observation window; measurable reduction in Loading + Flight Ops FTE hours on in-scope step types vs baseline; reduced IROPS-driven CSC handle time on in-scope events. | Backend: 1 | Q3 2026 | TBD | Process owners are available to define the automation rules; targets are stable enough to automate against. |
| CS-26H2-05 | SFS / Fidelio | Operational excellence |  |  | **Description:** Stabilise SFS / Fidelio integration. Investigation needed to scope. Dedicate a standalone investigation project. **Deliveries:** Investigation project output; stabilisation plan; prioritised remediation backlog. **Goal:** By the end of Q3 2026, deliver an investigation output that names the SFS/Fidelio integration's root failure modes, a stabilisation plan with named owners, and a prioritised remediation backlog ready for Q4 execution. **Success:** root cause(s) of SFS/Fidelio instability documented and signed off by Platform + Automation leads; stabilisation plan covers identified failure modes with named owners and effort estimates; prioritised remediation backlog ready for backlog grooming. | Backend: 2 Automation: 1 for investigation | Q3 2026 | TBD | Scope is not yet known; investigation precedes any commitment to delivery dates. Discovery of potential systems involved (Salesforce potentially) |
| CS-26H2-06 | New payment methods | Grow revenue | Sales |  | **Description:** Add Apple Pay, Google Pay and Vipps as payment methods. **Deliveries:** Apple Pay, Google Pay and Vipps integrated and available at checkout.  **Goal:** By the end of Q3 2026, Apple Pay, Google Pay and Vipps are selectable at checkout in production, capturing a measurable share of completed bookings and reducing payment-step abandonment vs the pre-launch baseline. **Success:** Apple Pay, Google Pay and Vipps each live and selectable at production checkout; instrumentation reports share of completed bookings using each method weekly; payment-step abandonment trend negative vs a 4-week pre-launch baseline. | Backend: 1 | Q3 2026 |  | Treasury department approval Commercial department prioritization.  |
| CS-26H2-07 | Set up Marketing Consent Preference model incl Double Opt-In | One Customer | CRM,  |  | **Description:** Backend SF readiness to enable Preference Center & Double Opt-in strategies  **Deliveries:** Adoption and migration to Salesforce Preference Model  **Goal:** By the end of Q4 2026, Salesforce is the system of record for Marketing Consent preferences (channels, content, frequency) and Double Opt-In flows, providing the backend substrate for CS-26-H2-10 Preference Centre. **Success:** Salesforce Preference Model live with consent fields, channel/content/frequency preferences, and Double Opt-In workflow; opted-in contacts migrated to the SF model for in-scope markets; CS-26-H2-10 Preference Cent**re** reads and writes against the model in production; no marketing consent state held outside the SF model post-migration. | SF: 2 SFMC: 2

| CS-26H2-09 | Lighthouse: Phase 2 | Grow revenue Operational excellence |  | <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-5">https://hurtigruten.atlassian.net/browse/SQSF-6023</custom>  | **Description:** Misc improvements to support Sales Delivery teams in Tallinn **Deliveries:**  **Teams:** Sales/Service, IVR, Salesforce **Goal:** By the end of Q4 2026, Lighthouse Phase 2 delivers a business-agreed, prioritised stream of improvements supporting Sales Delivery teams in Tallinn within the SF Core 2-3 FTE envelope, with explicit scope discipline replacing 'everything'-mode demand. **Success:** quarterly prioritisation cadence agreed with Jude and Sales Delivery; rolling visible backlog; delivery throughput tracked per quarter (count + impact); business feedback signal trending positive each quarter; demand explicitly bounded each quarter (no 'everything' mode). | SF Core: 2-3 | Q3-Q4 2026 | Potential backend support needed. Unclear.  | Scope is unclear; the business wants “everything” |
| CS-26-H2-10 | Preference Center Adoption on Email / Web | CRM Programme | CRM |  | **Description:**  Implement preference centre to enable customers to define contact channel, content & frequency  **-** <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-6">https://hurtigruten.atlassian.net/browse/DEMAND-183</custom>  **Deliveries:** Customer Preference Centre via Web & Email Footers **Teams:** SF, SFMC & Digital Products  **Goal:** By the end of Q4 2026, customers manage their marketing contact preferences (channel, content, frequency) via a Preference Centre surfaced on Web and Email Footers, reading and writing against the Salesforce Preference Model. **Success:** Preference Centre live on Web and in Email; preferences round-trip to SF Preference Model; opt-out and channel-change rates reflect customer agency rather than complaint volume; CS-26H2-07 backend confirmed as system of record. | SF Core: 1 SFMC: 2 | Q3-Q4 2026 | CS-26H2-07 | Assuming Michelle & Jenny still want to this.  |
| CS-26-H2-11 | PG SF Person Account Integration improvements (ARM)  | One Customer |  | <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-7">https://hurtigruten.atlassian.net/browse/SQSF-5570</custom>  | **Description:** Salesforce integration that synchronises customer profile data from PG (Polar Global) to Salesforce Person Accounts. **Deliveries:**  **Teams:** Salesforce, PG  Relates to  CS-26H2-01 **Goal:** By the end of Q3 2026, the PG-to-Salesforce Person Account integration synchronises customer profile data reliably under the ARM (Account Read Model) pattern, with measured data freshness and zero divergence between PG and SF on in-scope profile fields. **Success:** PG-to-SF profile sync running with the documented freshness SLO; profile-field divergence reported and trending toward zero on in-scope fields; the integration supports CS-26H2-01 ownership transfer as the read-model substrate. | SF Core: 1 (Pawel) Backend : 1 | Q1-Q3 2026 |  |  |
| CS-26-H2-12 | AirPort Express Automation for B2B | Operational excellence |  |  | **Description:** Follow-up from the B2C version, enables Flytoget ticketing automation, reducing CSC workload **Deliveries:**  Automated ticketing process **Teams:** SF, SFMC, CSC & CX **Goal:** By the end of Q4 2026, B2B AirPort Express (Flytoget) ticketing is automated end-to-end, eliminating CSC manual touchpoints for the in-scope booking flow. **Success:** automated ticketing live for B2B Flytoget bookings; CSC manual interventions on in-scope tickets trending to zero; SFMC comms triggered on automation events; B2B-side confirmation of ticket delivery and payment. | SF: 1 SFMC 2 | Q4 2026 | - | - |
| CS-26-H2-13 | Salesforce Comms Triggers | CRM Programme | CRM? |  | **Description:**  Adoption of ‘Contact Communication Events’ (CCE) as a trigger source for some SFMC campaigns  **Deliveries:** SF Support in development and testing of CCE **Teams:**  SF, SFMC & CX **Goal:** By the end of Q3 2026, Contact Communication Events (CCE) in Salesforce will trigger an agreed-upon set of SFMC campaigns, with end-to-end traceability from the event source to the customer touchpoint. **Success:** CCE wired to Salesforce; at least N in-scope SFMC campaigns triggered by CCE events; event-to-send latency within agreed SLO; CX team validates triggered campaigns hit the right cohorts. | SF:1-2 SFMC: 1 CX: 1 | Q3 2026 | Customer Engagement: Strategy and activation  | - |
| CS-26-H2-14 | Salesforce Data Support | One Customer | DACH |  | **Description:** Mobile Number Verification & Cleansing & DACH B2B UnSub Bug **Deliveries:**  Cleansed Mobile Numbers & DACH B2B Stabilised   **Teams:** SF & SFMC **Goal:** By the end of Q4 2026, two Salesforce data-quality issues will be resolved: mobile numbers verified and cleansed across the in-scope dataset, and the DACH B2B unsubscribe bug will be fixed in production. **Success:** percentage of contacts with verified mobile numbers above the agreed threshold; cleansing run on the full dataset with an audit log; DACH B2B unsubscribe bug fixed in production; no recurrence in the 4 weeks following the fix. |  SF:1 SFMC: 1 | Q4 2026 | - | - |
| CS-26-H2-15 | CSC Sales & Groups Live Reporting   | Operational excellence | Sales & Service |  | **Description:** Real-time monitoring dashboards of team performance in case resolution and sales  **Deliveries:** Production of live dashboards **Teams:** SF, Data Cloud & NO S&S Team **Goal:** By the end of Q3 2026, CSC Sales and Groups team leads run their daily and weekly cadence from live dashboards (case resolution and sales performance) rather than batch reports. **Success:** live dashboards for case resolution and sales in production; refresh latency within agreed SLO; NO Sales and Service team adopts the dashboards in their daily/weekly standups; batch-report consumption trends down. | SF:1-2 Data Cloud: 1 | Q3 2026 |  | - |
